what: Cached fusion-frontier recall re-tabulated against the PRODUCTION baseline instead of dense-only.
why: Every prior table in the campaign compared fusion variants to dense-only retrieval. Production does not serve dense-only: src/kb/kb.c ships kb_fusion_mode='rrf' with RRF_K=60 and 50 candidates per leg, which is exactly the 'rrf60' row. Comparing to dense overstates what a change would deliver and hides which variants regress.
note: This is a re-tabulation of cached measurements, not a new measurement run. No embedding or retrieval was re-executed.
findings: rrf10 is a strict Pareto improvement over production: nothing regresses on either embedder, and the R@1 delta is identically +0.0070 for both. Against production there is no top-1 cost to protect against - a framing error in earlier summaries, which described 'tiered' as the safe version of rrf10.

tiered and rrf10 are a genuine tradeoff, not a safety ladder. tiered takes 2.5x rrf10's R@1 gain (+0.0176 vs +0.0070) but a fifth of its R@10 gain (+0.0074 vs +0.0366). tiered's R@1 equals dense's exactly, by construction.

score-fusion variants (score50) are dominated by rrf10 on every metric and additionally regress R@50. The campaign flagged these rows as indicative rather than exact, because stage 1 persisted candidate ids but not scores.

unmeasured_and_worth_measuring.variant: tiered ordering at rank 1 with rrf_k=10 for ranks 2+
unmeasured_and_worth_measuring.rationale: Plausibly captures dense's R@1 (tiered's strength) and most of rrf10's R@10 gain. Never measured; the two were only evaluated as alternatives.
unmeasured_and_worth_measuring.blocked_on: Requires re-running the dense leg over eval/frozen-ab-v1 (26,473 docs + 10,000 queries). The per-query candidate lists from the original run were not persisted, and the host running this analysis has no GPU and no cached nomic weights. Needs the campaign's RTX 5080 environment.

standing_caveats_from_the_campaign: Suite queries appear lexically derived from their documents, which flatters BM25. rrf_k=10 sharpens the rank discount on both legs symmetrically, but if BM25's top-rank quality is what the suite inflates, k=10 amplifies that artifact. Direction of the effect is safe; magnitude is uncertain.
Labels are silver with one positive per query out of 26,473 documents. Absolute R@1 is not interpretable as accuracy; relative comparisons hold because all methods saw identical labels.
